title: LNG gas fuel supply system safety arrangements
plain: Do you know the procedures for checking and testing the gas fuel supply safety systems, and are they in good order?
why: Boil-off gas piped into the engine room can leak, ignite or explode if the safety systems are not working.
checks: The company procedure for inspecting, testing and maintaining the gas fuel safety arrangements
Records of inspection, maintenance and testing
The physical condition of the gas fuel system in the engine room
Whether you can explain how the safety systems work
ready: Procedure from the planned maintenance system or Cargo System Operation Manual
Test and maintenance records for leak and gas detection
Records for master gas fuel valve tests, automatic and manual
Ventilation and annular space inerting records
Gas detector alarm settings list
traps: No company procedure for inspection, testing and maintenance
Officer not familiar with annular space inerting or ventilation
Officer not familiar with leak detection or master valve operation
Tests not done as the company requires
Gas detector not set to alarm at 30% LFL and shut the master valve at no more than 60% LFL
Any safety arrangement defective or not working
say: Our SMS has a procedure for testing the gas fuel safety systems, and I can show you the records. The gas detectors alarm at 30% LFL and shut the master gas fuel valve at no more than 60% LFL. I can explain the annular space ventilation or inerting, leak detection and how the master valves close, automatically and by hand.

practice.q: What happens if gas is detected in the engine room spaces with gas consumers?
a: Alarm at 30% LFL
Master gas fuel valve shuts at no more than 60% LFL
Gas fuel line is inerted and gas freed as per procedure

practice.q: How is the annular space of the double wall gas pipe kept safe?
a: Either inert gas pressure or exhaust ventilation
Monitored and tested as per our procedure
Loss of protection leads to shutdown

practice.q: Show me how the master gas fuel valve is tested.
a: Test both automatic and manual closure
Record the result in the planned maintenance system

tip: Walk the gas fuel line once with the 2/E before the inspection so you can point to each safety item, not just read the procedure.

title: Cold spots and cofferdam heating
plain: Do you know how the hull is protected from cold, and are the temperature monitoring and cofferdam heating working?
why: If cargo or insulation leaks, the cold steel hull can crack (brittle fracture), so cold must be spotted early.
checks: Company procedure for protecting the hull from low temperature
Records of inner hull temperature readings and cold spot inspections
Condition and alarm settings of the inner hull temperature system
Condition of cofferdam heating, where fitted
ready: The procedure, possibly inside the Cargo System Operation Manual
Inner hull temperature reading records
Records of visual cold spot checks and any cold spots with action taken
Alarm setting list for the temperature system
Cofferdam heating maintenance records
traps: No procedure covering roles, cold spot detection, alarms, heating and records
Officer not sure what to do if a cold spot is found
Officer not sure what to do if cofferdam temperature falls below 5 degrees C or the stated limit
Officer not sure what to do if cofferdam heating fails
No records of readings, visual checks or cold spot actions
Temperature alarms wrongly set or inhibited
Cofferdam temperature not kept as the company requires
say: Our procedure explains who monitors the inner hull temperatures and what to do if a cold spot appears. I can show the readings and visual inspection records. If cofferdam temperature drops below the stated limit or the heating fails, we follow the procedure and inform the Master.

practice.q: What would you do if you found a cold spot?
a: Report to the Master straight away
Follow the company procedure
Record the cold spot and action taken

practice.q: What is your cofferdam temperature limit and what if it falls below?
a: Use the limit in our procedure (for example 5 degrees C or as stated)
Check heating, act as per procedure, record it

practice.q: What do you do if the cofferdam heating fails?
a: Follow the procedure for heating failure
Inform the Master
Keep records

tip: Know the alarm settings by heart and check that none are inhibited before the inspector arrives.

title: Cargo tank overfill alarms
plain: Do you know how the high-level and overfill alarms are tested and set, and are they working and set correctly?
why: These alarms are the last barrier before a cargo tank is overfilled.
checks: Company procedure for maintenance, setting and testing of the alarms
Test and maintenance records
Alarm panel in the cargo control room: on, all tanks monitored, audible and visible alarms working
Alarms on deck, where fitted
The document with maximum loading limits for each tank and product
ready: Procedure, with set points, test frequency and override controls
Test records before cargo operations and after dry-dock or decommissioning
Document of maximum allowable loading limits per tank, product and temperature
Maintenance records following the manufacturer's instructions
Risk assessment procedure for alarm failure during cargo work
traps: No company procedure, or missing items like set points, test frequency, override controls
Overfill alarms set above the maximum allowable loading limit
Alarms not set as company procedure requires
Alarms not in operation, or overridden, during cargo transfer
No test records before cargo operations or after dry-dock
Loading limits document not on board
Officer not familiar with when alarms may be isolated and the safeguards
Alarm system defective
say: Our procedure makes the overfill alarms mandatory for all loading, discharging and transfers. I can show the set points, the pre-operation test records and the loading limit document. Override is only for exceptional cases, controlled by the procedure and a risk assessment.

practice.q: When can the overfill alarm be overridden?
a: Only in exceptional circumstances, for example an overfilled tank that must be discharged
Only as the company procedure and risk assessment allow
Safeguards must keep protection in place

practice.q: How and when are the alarms tested?
a: Function test before cargo operations
Manufacturer's instructions and our test frequency
Records kept

practice.q: What if one tank alarm fails during loading?
a: Follow the risk-assessed procedure
Inform the Master
Do not continue unless the procedure allows it

tip: Keep the loading limits document next to the alarm test records in the CCR so both are ready together.

title: Cargo transfer ESD system
plain: Do the officers and cargo ratings know the ESD system, and is it tested, maintained and working?
why: ESD stops cargo flow in an emergency, so a leak or fire does not get worse.
checks: Company procedure for operation, inspection, maintenance and testing of ESD
Pre-arrival test checklist and timing and sequencing checklist
Cause and effect flowcharts in the CCR and on the bridge
Push buttons, fire detection or fusible plugs on deck, and an ESD manifold valve
A cargo rating: do they know where the manual ESD controls are and when to use them
ready: Procedure and Cargo System Operation Manual section on ESD
Checklist for the last pre-arrival ESD test
Records of ESD valve closing time checks and sequencing
Functional flowcharts posted in CCR and on the bridge
Planned maintenance records that match what was actually done
Contingency plan if the ship/shore link is not available
traps: Flowchart not posted in the CCR and on the bridge
ESD and ship/shore link status not clearly visible in the CCR
Fusible elements painted over
Push buttons blocked or not ready for use
No records of ESD checks before cargo handling or of timing and sequencing
Valve closing time information not on board
Rating does not know where the manual ESD controls are
Officer not clear on who may authorise inhibiting and how it is reinstated
Planned maintenance shows work that was not done
No contingency plan for ship/shore link failure
say: I know our ESD initiators, such as push buttons, fire detection, high level and blackout, and what they shut down. I can show the flowchart, the pre-arrival test checklist and the closing time records. Any inhibit needs authorisation and must be reinstated immediately afterwards.

practice.q: What can trigger the ESD?
a: Emergency push buttons
Fire detection on deck
High tank level, loss of power or ship/shore link signal

practice.q: When can ESD be inhibited and who allows it?
a: Only for short periods such as testing
Authorised by the person named in our procedure
Reinstated immediately after

practice.q: Rating question: where are the manual ESD buttons and when do you press them?
a: Know the locations on deck, in CCR and on the bridge
Press in an emergency such as leak, fire or spill

tip: Take your cargo ratings to each ESD push button before the inspection so they can point to them without hesitation.

title: Cargo tank relief valves
plain: Do you know how cargo tank relief valves are inspected, tested, set and isolated if faulty?
why: A relief valve that sticks or leaks can over-pressure or damage a cargo tank.
checks: Company procedure for inspection, maintenance, testing and setting
Records of checks, six-monthly inspections, annual free operation tests and five-yearly overhaul
Records of any change of set pressure
The valves and vent masts on deck: seals, paint, corrosion, water in the riser
ready: Procedure, with the response to a valve malfunction including isolation
Records of checks before each cargo operation
Six-monthly visual inspection and annual field test kit records, where applicable
Five-yearly overhaul records
Setting change records, with signs showing the setting in force
Training evidence for the officer responsible
traps: No procedure, or officer not familiar with changing set pressure and resetting alarms
Records missing for pre-cargo checks, six-monthly, annual or five-yearly work
Valve seals missing or broken
No records or no sign for a changed pressure setting
Isolated defective valve with no record or no sign in the CCR or at the valve
Tank loaded with a defective, isolated valve
Valve painted so it may not work, or galvanic corrosion
Rainwater in vent masts or vent drains left open
Responsible officer not trained as company procedure requires
say: Our procedure covers checks before each cargo operation, six-monthly inspections, annual free operation tests and the five-yearly overhaul, all recorded. Seals are intact and settings are displayed. If a valve fails, we isolate it as per procedure, record it and post a sign.

practice.q: What do you do if a relief valve malfunctions?
a: Isolate only one relief valve on the tank, as per procedure, under the Master's supervision
Record it in the ship's log and post a sign in the CCR and at the valve
Do not load that tank until full relieving capacity is restored

practice.q: How do you change the set pressure?
a: Under the Master's supervision, as per the approved procedure
Record the change in the ship's log
Reset the high pressure alarm and post the setting in the CCR and at each valve

practice.q: How often is the valve checked?
a: Each cargo operation, six-monthly, annually where applicable
Five-yearly overhaul

tip: Check the vent mast drains are closed and no water has collected before the inspector walks the deck.

title: Cargo System Operation Manual
plain: Is there a ship-specific Cargo System Operation Manual on board, and do officers know what is in it?
why: Officers need clear, approved ship-specific instructions to run the cargo system safely.
checks: The manual is on board
It is ship specific and covers dock to dock operation
It covers all contents the IGC Code lists
It is approved and in a language the officers understand
Whether the accompanying officer knows its contents
ready: The approved manual (it may be several documents)
Evidence of flag or class approval
Sections on loading limits, pressure and temperature control, ESD and emergency procedures
Information on maximum loading rates
Hazards and properties of every cargo the ship may carry
traps: No manual on board
Manual not ship specific
Does not cover hazards and properties of all permitted cargoes
Does not cover the dock to dock operating cycle or describe the equipment
No maximum loading rate information
Not approved by flag or a recognised organisation
Officer not familiar with the contents
Manual not in a language the officers understand
say: Our ship-specific Cargo System Operation Manual is in the CCR and approved by the flag or recognised organisation. It covers the whole dock to dock cycle, system limits, ESD, gas detection and emergency procedures. I can show you where to find any section.

practice.q: Where would you find the procedure to change relief valve settings?
a: In the Cargo System Operation Manual
Show the section

practice.q: What are the cargo system limits?
a: Minimum temperatures, maximum pressures
Transfer rates, filling and sloshing limits

practice.q: What emergency procedures does the manual cover?
a: Relief valve isolation
Single tank gas freeing and entry
Emergency ship-to-ship transfer

tip: Mark the key sections with tabs so you can find them quickly during questioning.

title: Interbarrier and hold space atmosphere
plain: Do you know how the containment system is monitored and how the interbarrier and hold space atmosphere is kept safe, with records?
why: A leak or wrong atmosphere in these spaces can cause fire, damage to insulation or an unseen cargo tank leak.
checks: Company procedure: parameters, acceptable ranges, set points and actions if out of range
Records of the parameters monitored and actions taken
Nitrogen consumption and nitrogen generator running hours
Nitrogen purging arrangements and sweeping valve positions
Whether you can explain the procedure
ready: Procedure, possibly inside the Cargo System Operation Manual
Records of pressure, temperature, flammable gas, oxygen and dew point, as applicable
Nitrogen consumption and generator running hours records
Alarm set point list
Record of actions taken to keep the atmosphere correct
traps: No procedure covering roles, parameters, ranges, actions, set points and records
Atmosphere not kept as company requires for pressure, temperature, gas, oxygen or dew point
No records of nitrogen consumption and generator running hours
Interbarrier pressure too low to keep outside air out
Monitoring equipment defective or alarms inhibited or wrongly set
Hold spaces without open connection to atmosphere have no suitable pressure gauges
Low secondary barrier temperature reading, which may mean liquid cargo on the barrier
Sweeping valves left open after purging
say: Our procedure lists the parameters we monitor, their acceptable ranges and what to do if one goes out of range. I can show you the records, nitrogen consumption and alarm set points. Sweeping valves are closed after purging, because an open one can point to a gas leak.

practice.q: Why do you watch nitrogen consumption?
a: Higher use can show a leak into the space
Trend it and record it

practice.q: What do you do if a parameter is out of range?
a: Take the action in our procedure
Inform the Master
Record the action

practice.q: What does a sweeping valve found open tell you?
a: It may indicate gas leakage into the primary space
Should be closed when not purging

tip: Trend the readings on one sheet so changes between loaded and ballast passage are easy to explain.

title: Cargo system alarm management
plain: Do you know the rules for managing cargo alarms, including who can change set points or override an alarm?
why: Alarms that are changed or overridden without control can hide real danger.
checks: Company procedure for managing and operating cargo alarm systems
Records of set point changes and alarm overrides
Risk assessment, authorisation and time limits on those records
Password and key control for changing set points or overriding
Whether you can explain the procedure
ready: Alarm management procedure with roles and responsibilities
Records of every set point change and override
Risk assessments and authorisations for them
Instructions for when an alarm is temporarily out of service
Control of passwords and keys by the persons named in the procedure
traps: No procedure covering roles, authorisation, risk assessment, alarm out of service and records
Procedure does not match the controls fitted on board
Passwords or keys freely available, not controlled
Officer not familiar with the procedure
No or incomplete records, for example no risk assessment
Alarm found overridden or disabled with no risk assessment or authorisation on record
say: Under our procedure, only named persons can change a set point or override an alarm, and only after risk assessment and authorisation. Time limits are set, and everything is recorded. Passwords and keys are controlled by those named in the procedure.

practice.q: Who can change a cargo alarm set point?
a: Only persons named in our procedure
After risk assessment and authorisation
Record it

practice.q: What if an alarm is temporarily out of service?
a: Follow the interim actions in the procedure
Record it
Return to service after repair and test

practice.q: Who holds the password or key for overrides?
a: Persons named in the procedure
Not freely available

tip: Check that the override log matches what the system shows right now, with nothing inhibited that is not recorded.
refs: SIGTTO Management of Cargo Alarm Systems 2019

title: Inert gas system on gas carriers
plain: Do you know how the inert gas or nitrogen system is run, tested and kept, and is it in good condition?
why: Wrong quality inert gas can damage the cargo system, and leaks or exhaust can hurt people.
checks: Company procedure for operation, inspection, testing and maintenance
Records of inspection, testing, maintenance and checks before, during and after operation
Records of oxygen and pressure checks in tanks, holds and interbarrier spaces
The plant itself, oxygen meter calibration, non-return valves, warning signs
Whether you know the nitrogen generator hazards
ready: Procedure with a description of the system, roles, CO2 and dew point limits
Oxygen meter calibration records following the manufacturer's instructions
Non-return valve test records
Records of oxygen monitoring in spaces with generators or nitrogen equipment
Warning signs and safe entry procedure posted at plant room entrances
traps: No procedure covering the listed items, or officer not familiar with it
Oxygen meter not calibrated per the manufacturer
Non-return valves not tested at regular intervals
No records of checks or of oxygen and pressure checks
No evidence of oxygen monitoring in spaces that may become oxygen deficient
No safe entry procedure posted at the plant room entrances
Inert gas unsuitable: not compatible, dew point too high, oxygen over 5% (or the lower limit for peroxide forming cargoes), CO2 too high
Spool pieces left connected between inert gas and cargo systems
Officer unaware of oxygen deficiency or oxygen-rich exhaust from the nitrogen generator
say: Our procedure describes the inert gas plant, who operates it and how it is checked and maintained. I can show the oxygen meter calibration, non-return valve tests and the records of oxygen and pressure checks. I know nitrogen can cause oxygen deficiency, and the generator exhaust is oxygen-rich.

practice.q: What oxygen limit applies to the inert gas?
a: Not above 5%
Lower limit for cargoes that can form peroxides, as in our procedure

practice.q: What are the dangers around a nitrogen generator?
a: Oxygen deficient air if nitrogen leaks
Oxygen-rich exhaust is a flammability and safety hazard

practice.q: How do you stop cargo vapour flowing back into the inert gas plant?
a: Non-return valves tested regularly
Temporary connections removed and blanked after use

tip: Check the warning signs at the plant room doors and take any spool piece off before the inspector looks.

title: Gas carrier cargo manifolds
plain: Do you know how cargo and vapour connections at the manifold are managed, and is the manifold area in good condition?
why: Leaks at the manifold can release flammable, very cold or toxic cargo on deck.
checks: Company procedure for managing cargo and vapour connections
Manifold area: bolting, blanks, gauges, drip trays, supports, strainers, exits, marking
LNG: disconnection procedure and gas meter used to verify before disconnection
A deck rating on manifold watch: low temperature hazards and signs of leakage
Class certified manifold load and pressure rating information
ready: The procedure, with LNG disconnection steps where relevant
Class certified allowable loads and pressure ratings for manifold, flanges, reducers and spool pieces
Meter calibrated for methane in nitrogen (LNG)
Blanks fitted on unused connections, vents, drains and sample points
Safe working loads marked on the manifold, liquid and vapour clearly marked
traps: No procedure, or officer not familiar with it
LNG: no detailed disconnection procedure, or meter not calibrated for methane in nitrogen
LNG: officer unsure of the manifold drain line and remote opening
Rating unsure of low temperature hazards or leak signs
Strainer by-passed, or officer unsure how to monitor pressure across the filter
Damaged or wrong bolts, missing bolts, G-clamps, camlocks not engaged
Loading arm jacks on oil drums or on gratings not designed for the load
Blank flanges not as thick, not documented, or not fully bolted
Unused manifold not blanked, or leaking
No drip tray, drains not valved and capped, or water in an LNG drip tray
Hull water curtain not running during LNG transfer
Midships crane used for stores during cargo, or non-essential people not kept out
say: Our procedure covers hose or arm connection, blanks, gauges, drip trays and, on LNG carriers, step by step disconnection. All unused connections are blanked and fully bolted. My watch ratings know the low temperature hazards and how to spot a leak.

practice.q: How do you know the manifold is safe to disconnect on an LNG carrier?
a: Drain, isolate, remove liquid and purge
Verify target gas concentration with a meter calibrated for methane in nitrogen
Then disconnect

practice.q: Rating question: what would tell you a manifold is leaking?
a: Frosting on the valve or flange
Gas detector alarm at the manifold
Report to the cargo officer and stop operation as per procedure

practice.q: Why must the LNG drip tray stay dry?
a: Water in a spill can cause rapid phase transition
Do not add water and do not let rain collect

tip: Walk the manifold with a rating before the inspection and look for loose blanks, missing caps and water in the drip tray.
refs: SIGTTO LNG MLA Draining, Purging and Disconnection

title: Manifold reducers, spool pieces and portable pipework
plain: Do you know how reducers and spool pieces are used, stored, tested and inspected, and are they in good condition?
why: A reducer with a lower pressure rating or damaged flange can leak cargo at the manifold.
checks: Company procedure for use, inspection and testing
Inventory of reducers, spool pieces and other portable pipework
Inspection records and test certificates
Condition of flange faces, with blanks or covers removed from at least one stored item
How items are fitted and supported when in use
ready: Procedure with correct use, certification, storage and inspection guidance
Full inventory of reducers, spool pieces, Y pieces and spiders
Test certificates for each item, showing the same or higher rating as fixed manifold piping
Inspection records
Evidence of pressure testing after any repair
Material suitable for the minimum cargo temperature in the Certificate of Fitness
traps: No procedure or no inventory
No test certificate for an item
No inspection records, or inspections not effective
Rating (MAWP) lower than the fixed manifold piping
Handles or lugs in the way of quick coupling or flange bolting
More than one reducer or spool piece between manifold flange and connection
Flange face damaged, corroded or pitted
Long spool piece not supported
Repaired item with no pressure test
Material not suitable for the minimum cargo temperature
say: We keep an inventory of every reducer and spool piece, each with test certification showing the rating matches the manifold piping. They are stored with flange faces protected and inspected regularly as per our procedure. Only one reducer or spool piece is fitted between the manifold flange and the connection.

practice.q: What rating must a reducer have?
a: The same or greater certified rating as the fixed manifold piping
Certificate on board

practice.q: How are they stored?
a: Flange faces protected by covers
Inspected regularly and recorded

practice.q: Can you fit two reducers together?
a: No, only one between manifold flange and connection
Long pieces must be supported

tip: Match each item's number on the inventory to its certificate and stowage position so you can find any of them fast.

title: Emergency discharge operations
plain: Do you know how to discharge cargo if equipment fails, and is any emergency equipment in good condition?
why: If cargo pumps fail, the ship must still be able to get the cargo out safely.
checks: Ship-specific company procedure for emergency discharge
Whether you can explain the method for your ship type
Emergency cargo pump condition, storage and records, where carried
Pressurisation procedure with relief valve resetting, where used
ready: Emergency discharge procedure in the Cargo System Operation Manual
Emergency pump inspection and test records, where fitted
Emergency pump stored in a dry (nitrogen) atmosphere
Relief valve resetting guidance where emergency transfer is by pressurisation
Eductor drive medium and contamination guidance, where used
traps: No ship-specific procedure for emergency discharge
Officer not familiar with the procedure
Emergency pump defective
Emergency pump not stored in the required dry atmosphere
No inspection and test records for the emergency pump
Pressurisation procedure does not say how to reset relief valves
say: Our procedure is ship specific and explains how we would discharge if cargo pumps failed. For our system it covers preparing, fitting, running and storing the emergency pump, or pressurisation with relief valve resetting. Inspection and test records are on board.

practice.q: What would you do if both cargo pumps in a tank failed?
a: Follow the emergency discharge procedure
Use the emergency pump or pressurisation, depending on ship type
Inform the Master

practice.q: How is the emergency pump kept ready?
a: Stored in its special case with a dry atmosphere
Inspected and tested as per procedure

practice.q: If discharging by pressurisation, what must you remember?
a: Resetting the tank relief valves where necessary
Follow set pressure limits in the procedure

tip: Know which method your ship type uses, since the inspector will expect only that one explained properly.

title: Cargo and vapour pipeline insulation and expansion
plain: Do you know how cargo and vapour line insulation and expansion arrangements are inspected, and are they in good condition?
why: Damaged insulation or stuck expansion parts can cause cold damage, corrosion, leaks or pipe stress.
checks: Company procedure for regular inspection and maintenance
Inspection and maintenance records, including repairs
Insulation and covers on deck lines
Bellows, bends or loops, pipe supports, clamps and insulating chocks
ready: Procedure or planned maintenance entries covering all cargo and vapour lines
Inspection records with repair details
Insulation intact with no sections missing
Bellows undamaged, free of tie-bars, with sleeves in place
Chocks of the right material and none missing
traps: No procedure, or work not done as the procedure says
Insulation removed and not replaced, or cracked or damaged
Icing on insulation, showing local failure
Corrosion under insulation
Bellows with cracks, corrosion, pin holes or wear
Temporary tie-bars left on bellows, or flexible sleeve missing
Pipe not free to move in clamps
Chocks of wrong material or missing
say: Our planned maintenance covers all cargo and vapour lines, including insulation, bellows and supports. I can show the inspection records and any repairs. We watch for icing, damaged insulation and anything stopping pipes from moving freely.

practice.q: What does icing on insulation tell you?
a: A local insulation failure
Report it and repair as per procedure

practice.q: What do you check on bellows?
a: Cracks, corrosion, pin holes and wear
No temporary tie-bars left on
Protective sleeve fitted

practice.q: Why must pipes be free in their clamps?
a: They must expand and contract with temperature
Stuck pipes build stress

tip: Walk the main deck line once before the inspection, looking for icing marks, torn covers and left-on tie-bars.

title: IGC safety, rescue and recovery equipment
plain: Do you know the company rules for the IGC safety equipment, SCBA and resuscitators, and is it all ready for immediate use?
why: If someone collapses in a gas-filled space, rescuers need working breathing apparatus and rescue gear at once.
checks: Company procedure for stowing, inspecting and using the safety equipment
SCBA records: monthly officer inspection and annual test by a competent person
At least one full safety equipment set, plus the stretcher and oxygen resuscitator
Firefighter outfits: five if the ship is over 5000 cubic metres cargo capacity
Who did the annual SCBA service and their manufacturer training certificate
ready: Procedure covering stowage, SCBA inspection, non-emergency use limits and resuscitator use
Monthly inspection records logged, and annual test records
Enough complete sets: at least three for ships delivered after 01 July 2016, two before
Each set: SCBA with full face mask (1,200 litres of free air), gastight suit, boots, gloves, steel-cored line with belt, explosion-proof lamp
Spare charged bottle for each SCBA, compressor and charging manifold
Suit suitability for all cargoes on the Certificate of Fitness and for flammable atmosphere
traps: No procedure covering stowage, inspection, non-emergency use limits and oxygen resuscitator
Officer not familiar with the procedure
Fewer sets than required, or a set missing an item
No spare charged bottle, compressor or charging manifold
Protective suits not gastight, not suitable for the cargoes or not for flammable atmosphere
Annual SCBA service by a crew member with no valid manufacturer training certificate for that SCBA type
Resuscitator not in good condition or oxygen bottle not full
Monthly or annual SCBA records missing or incomplete
say: Our procedure covers where the equipment is kept, monthly checks, the annual service and limits on non-emergency use. I can show the records, a complete safety set, the stretcher and the resuscitator. Our crew member who services the SCBA holds the manufacturer's training certificate.

practice.q: What is in one complete IGC safety equipment set?
a: SCBA with full face mask, not using stored oxygen
Protective clothing, boots and gloves
Steel-cored rescue line with belt, and explosion-proof lamp

practice.q: How often are SCBAs inspected?
a: Monthly by a responsible officer, logged
Annually by a competent person

practice.q: Who can do the annual SCBA test onboard?
a: A crew member who did the manufacturer course for that SCBA type within the five years before the service
Needs the test equipment and the certificate kept with the records

tip: Keep the SCBA training certificate copy clipped into the annual service record, since inspectors look for it.

title: IGC protective equipment

checks: Company procedure and PPE matrix for the products and tasks
Inspection records and inventory of protective equipment
Stored equipment: condition, place and sizes
Protective equipment actually being worn on deck
A deck officer or rating showing how to pick and put on a full set including the suit
ready: Procedure with PPE list, matrix, training, fitness checks, time limits in suits, cleaning, storage and defect actions
Inventory and inspection records
SDS for the products handled
Chemical resistance list for the suits provided
Evidence that suits are suitable for flammable atmosphere
Enough equipment in all sizes for the crew
traps: No procedure, or missing items such as PPE matrix, training or inspection frequency
Officer not familiar with the procedure
Crew not wearing, or wearing wrongly, the protective clothing
Equipment does not give the protection the SDS requires
Safety spectacles used instead of splash protection for the eyes
Equipment stored in a poor place, or in an unauthorised space in the accommodation
No chemical resistance list, or no evidence suits suit flammable atmosphere
Gloves, boots or head gear weaker than the suit
Not enough equipment or sizes
Officer or rating cannot show how to select and put on a full set
say: Our procedure includes a PPE matrix showing what to wear for each task and product. Equipment is stored in a ventilated locker, inspected and recorded, and we have sizes for everyone. I can check the SDS and resistance list, and show how to put on a full suit.

practice.q: What eye protection do you use for splash risk?
a: Goggles with a face shield, not ordinary safety glasses
As the PPE matrix and SDS require

practice.q: How do you choose the right PPE for a cargo?
a: Check the SDS and the PPE matrix
Check the suit's chemical resistance list

practice.q: Show me how you put on a full chemical suit.
a: Check suit and fitness for the conditions first
Fit suit, gloves, boots, head gear and breathing apparatus correctly
Buddy check before entering the working area

tip: Practise donning a full suit with a rating before the inspection, so you can do it smoothly in front of the inspector.

title: Reliquefaction plant
plain: Do you know how the reliquefaction plant is operated and maintained safely, and is it in good condition?
why: A badly run plant can overfill receivers or condensers, damage machinery, or fail to control tank pressure.
checks: Company procedure for operation, testing and maintenance of the plant and its controls
Records of inspection, maintenance and testing, including relief valve tests
Records of regular liquid level checks in receivers and condensers
Compressor oil level, oil and refrigerant compatibility with cargo
Compressor discharge temperature limits
ready: Procedure with roles, system description, start-up and shut-down
Records of inspection, maintenance, pressure tests and instrument calibration
Safety relief valve test records
Records of regular liquid level checks during operation

say: Our procedure explains what to do on a fire or gas alarm in the BLS area, the alarm set point and how often we calibrate and test. I can show the calibration records, the in-date calibration gas, and that the panels show no faults. All sensors are in service.

practice.q: What do you do on a gas alarm in the BLS area?
a: Follow the procedure for gas alarm actions
Stop loading as the procedure requires and inform the Master

practice.q: How often are sensors calibrated?
a: As the company procedure sets, following manufacturer's instructions
Records kept

practice.q: What is the gas alarm set point?
a: The value in our procedure
Checked at the set frequency
